samples.summary: New single-definition URL builder validates every path segment but leaves `config.server` completely unvalidated, so an env/profile-supplied origin still receives the bearer credential (and, on 401, the refresh token)
samples.evidence: `origin(config)` (url.ts:44-46) only strips a trailing slash. Every request URL — including the credentialed ones — is `${origin(config)}${path}`, and `HttpClient.authHeaders` (http-client.ts:63-73) attaches `Authorization: Bearer <apiKey|accessToken>` unconditionally. `resolveConfig` (config/config.ts:90-94, 114-119) takes `server` from `--server`, then `WAFFLEBASE_SERVER`, then the *session* / YAML profile, with no requirement that it match the `session.server` the JWT was minted for and no scheme check. Attack: anything that can set `WAFFLEBASE_SERVER` for the user's shell (a project `.envrc`/direnv, a CI job config, a dotfile edit) silently redirects an already-logged-in session — the first request ships the access token to the attacker host, and `refreshSession()` (http-client.ts:96-101) then POSTs the long-lived **refresh token** to `${server}/auth/refresh` on that same host. `http://` origins are equally accepted, sending `wfb_…` API keys in cleartext. The PR centralises URL construction here, which is the natural (and now only) chokepoint for such a check; the segment guard added alongside it may read as 'URL construction is now hardened' when the origin half is not.
searchedFor: read packages/cli/src/config/config.ts resolveConfig for server precedence
read packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts and config/session.ts for where session.server is recorded vs used

samples.summary: The workspace/document path-segment invariant this PR establishes is CLI-only; the other client of the same routes interpolates router-supplied ids into the API URL with no escaping
samples.evidence: `url.ts` now makes 'every id interpolated into a workspace-scoped API URL is escaped, and dot segments are refused' an explicit security invariant for the CLI. The browser client of the same endpoints does not hold it: `packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/image-upload.ts:47` builds `${BACKEND_BASE}/api/v1/workspaces/${workspaceId}/images`, and `packages/frontend/src/api/folders.ts:10,24` and `api/miro.ts:93` build `${VITE_BACKEND_API_URL}/workspaces/${workspaceId}/...`, all with raw interpolation. `workspaceId` there comes from the route (react-router already percent-decodes params), so a crafted app link whose workspace param decodes to `../../x` makes the browser issue the credentialed request against a different API path than the one the code names. I did not trace a concrete privileged endpoint reachable this way, hence low confidence; flagging because the guard added here is easy to mistake for a repo-wide invariant. Out of the PR's file set — informational, not a blocker on this delta.
searchedFor: read packages/cli/src/client/url.ts to establish the invariant being generalised

samples.summary: `DOT_SEGMENT`'s `%2e` alternatives are unreachable because the test runs on the already-encoded value, so the doc comment claims coverage the code cannot exercise
samples.evidence: `seg()` (url.ts:31-41) computes `encodeURIComponent(value)` first and tests `DOT_SEGMENT` against the *encoded* string. `encodeURIComponent` escapes `%` to `%25`, so the encoded value can only ever be `.` or `..` — the `%2e`, `.%2e`, `%2e.`, `%2e%2e` branches the comment at url.ts:6-11 enumerates can never match. Behaviourally correct today (a raw `%2e%2e` input becomes `%252e%252e`, harmless data, as the new test asserts), but a future maintainer who moves the check before encoding, or who adds a caller that passes a pre-encoded id, would be relying on a branch whose coverage was never demonstrated. Worth a comment saying the `%2e` forms are defence-in-depth against a pre-encoded input, not the current path.

finding.summary: New `seg()` guard is incomplete: `encodeURIComponent` does not escape `.`, so a bare `..` identifier still triggers dot-segment resolution — `api-keys revoke ..` issues `DELETE /workspaces/<ws>/`, which matches the workspace-delete route
finding.evidence:
`seg()` (http-client.ts:32) is `encodeURIComponent`, which escapes `/` (`%2F`) but leaves `.` untouched: `encodeURIComponent('..') === '..'`. The comment at http-client.ts:23-30 claims every interpolated identifier is now safe from dot-segment resolution, but a segment that IS exactly `..` still resolves.

Chain: `wafflebase api-keys revoke ..` → api-keys.ts:76 → `revokeApiKey('..')` → http-client.ts:417 builds `${server}/workspaces/${ws}/api-keys/..` → `fetch` (line 418) normalises with the WHATWG parser to `${server}/workspaces/${ws}/` and sends DELETE with the caller's `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` (jsonHeaders). Backend: `packages/backend/src/workspace/workspace.controller.ts:57` declares `@Delete('workspaces/:id')` under `JwtAuthGuard`; Nest/Express run with `strict routing` disabled (no `set('strict routing', …)` in packages/backend/src/main.ts:31-41), so the trailing-slash path matches `:id`. `workspace.service.ts:83-92` then deletes the entire workspace (owner + >1 workspace).

So a key-id of `..` — a plausible value when the id comes from a script, an agent, or untrusted data — turns a scoped `revoke` into irreversible destruction of the whole workspace and its documents. The other `..`-reachable endpoints degrade to 404 (no bare `@Delete()`/`@Get()` on `api/v1/workspaces/:workspaceId`, no `@Delete(':tabId')`), so `/workspaces/:id` is the one live target. Fix: reject or escape dot segments (e.g. map `.`/`..` to `%2E`/`%2E%2E`, or validate the identifier) rather than relying on `encodeURIComponent` alone.

verdict.reason: The finding claims `seg()` is at http-client.ts:32 and is a bare `encodeURIComponent` that lets a literal `..` through. Neither is true. `seg()` is defined at packages/cli/src/client/url.ts:31-41 (http-client.ts:8 imports it; http-client.ts:32 is the `code: string;` field of the `ApiError` interface). The real implementation rejects dot segments: url.ts:13 defines `const DOT_SEGMENT = /^(?:\.|%2e){1,2}$/i;` and url.ts:33-39 throws when the encoded segment is empty or matches it — covering `.`, `..`, `%2e`, `.%2e`, `%2e.`, `%2e%2e` case-insensitively, exactly the WHATWG dot-segment set. The comment at url.ts:20-24 names this very attack ("`api-keys revoke ..` would become `DELETE /workspaces/<ws>/`") and states escaping handles `/`/`?` while rejection handles `..`. The claimed exploit chain breaks at its first link: api-keys.ts:75 -> http-client.ts:401-403 revokeApiKey -> apiKeysUrl (url.ts:60-63) -> seg(keyId) at url.ts:62 throws before the `fetch` on http-client.ts:403, and the error is caught at api-keys.ts:78-79; no credentialed DELETE is sent, so the backend routing analysis is moot. Glob confirms url.ts is the only such module under packages/cli/src, and the only other encodeURIComponent uses (http-client.ts:346, cells.ts:27, sheets-export.ts:49) are `?range=` query-string values where no dot-segment resolution occurs, so there is no unguarded path-interpolation call site.

finding.summary: `--dry-run` preview diverges from the request actually sent for a `..` identifier, and it diverges on exactly the destructive command the preview exists to protect
finding.evidence: `apiKeysUrl(opts, '..')` (api-keys.ts:17) prints `${server}/workspaces/<ws>/api-keys/..` because `seg('..') === '..'` (dry-run.ts:12-14). The live command sends the same string to `fetch`, which normalises it to `${server}/workspaces/<ws>/` — a DELETE that `packages/backend/src/workspace/workspace.controller.ts:57` serves as "delete workspace". An operator (or agent) who pre-flights `api-keys revoke ..` is shown a URL under `/api-keys/`, concludes the request is key-scoped, and then executes a workspace deletion. The same no-op applies to every `seg()` in dry-run.ts, so the invariant the header comment states ("the preview is the request") does not hold for `.`/`..` segments.

verdict.reason: The finding's central factual claim is false. It asserts `seg('..') === '..'` as a no-op defined at dry-run.ts:12-14. dry-run.ts:12-14 is actually the signature of `printDryRun(config, method, path, body?)`; dry-run.ts contains no `seg()` definition, only a doc-comment reference (dry-run.ts:8). The single definition of `seg()` is url.ts:31-41, and it explicitly REJECTS dot segments: url.ts:13 defines `DOT_SEGMENT = /^(?:\.|%2e){1,2}$/i` and url.ts:33-39 throws when the `encodeURIComponent` result is empty or matches it. `encodeURIComponent('..') === '..'` matches, so `seg('..')` throws; the case-insensitive regex also covers `.`, `%2e`, `.%2e`, `%2e.`, `%2e%2e`, and double-encoded `%252e%252e` is inert to the URL parser. Both the preview path (api-keys.ts:16 -> apiKeysUrl -> url.ts:62) and the live path (http-client.ts:402 -> apiKeysUrl -> url.ts:62) call that same `seg()`, so `api-keys revoke ..` throws before any fetch on both branches (dry-run throw caught by the try/catch at api-keys.ts:68-80; live throw at http-client.ts:402 precedes fetch at http-client.ts:403). No execution prints `/api-keys/..` or sends a normalised `DELETE /workspaces/<ws>/`. `config.workspace` is likewise guarded at url.ts:50 and url.ts:61. The described defective code is not present.
